questions.question: Name four questions geographers ask when classifying a climate, and explain why climates are classified.
questions.expected_answer: How hot is it, and is there a cold season? How large is the annual temperature range? How much rain falls in a year? When does the rain fall: all year, mainly summer or mainly winter? Classification groups thousands of stations into types, mainly using Köppen's system based on temperature and precipitation and matching vegetation. It helps farmers choose crops and livestock, architects design comfortable buildings, health authorities predict diseases such as malaria, and planners estimate water supply. Boundaries are gradual, and local factors such as altitude create pockets of different climate, as on the highveld.

questions.question: Describe the tropical rainforest and tropical savanna climates, including their location, temperature, rainfall and vegetation.
questions.expected_answer: Tropical rainforest: near the equator in the Congo and Amazon basins and South-East Asia; about 26 to 27 °C every month with a range of 1 to 3 °C; heavy rain, usually over 2 000 mm, in every month, often from afternoon convection storms, for example Kisangani about 1 800 mm with no dry month; dense evergreen rainforest with high biodiversity. Tropical savanna: roughly 5 to 20 degrees from the equator in much of Africa, including Zambia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique and the far north of South Africa, plus northern Australia, India and Brazil; hot all year with a slightly cooler season; a wet summer when the sun is overhead and a dry winter; about 500 to 1 500 mm; grassland with scattered trees such as acacias and baobabs, with large herds, as in the Serengeti and Kruger.

questions.question: Compare the humid subtropical climate of Durban with the temperate oceanic climate of London.
questions.expected_answer: Durban, humid subtropical, at about 30 degrees south on the east side of the continent beside the warm Agulhas: January about 24.5 °C, July about 17 °C, range about 7.5 °C; about 1 000 mm, mostly in summer with some every month; hot, humid summers and mild winters with rare frost; subtropical forest and grassland, sugar cane, bananas, citrus. London, temperate oceanic, at about 51 degrees north on the west side of Europe in the westerly belt: January about 5 °C, July about 19 °C, range about 14 °C; about 600 mm spread evenly as light rain and drizzle; cool summers, cold but not severe winters; deciduous forest, dairy, wheat and barley. London's higher latitude gives cooler temperatures and a larger range; its westerly ocean winds give all-year rain.
